findings.title: Persist the Blocked epoch transition under its original mutation ID
findings.problem: The unresolved/missing handover branch changes RouteControl.Phase to Blocked and inserts EpochBlocked audit, then returns PendingCommit without inserting OutboxLeaseMutationReceiptV2 for mutationId. A committed state change therefore has no original mutation result. Repeating the identical input reaches the changed root xmin check at line 37 and returns Conflict instead of the prior result; an original-key receipt lookup remains absent/Unknown.
reproduction: Seed a Pending row; BeginDrainV2 with switchId S and commit. Read the resulting control token V.

Make the trusted fixture Owner return UnknownTransactionsAuthoritativelyResolved=false. Call AdvanceEpochV2(M,S,epoch=1,V), observe PendingCommit/Blocked, actually commit, and suppress the application acknowledgement.

In a new transaction repeat exactly AdvanceEpochV2(M,S,1,V). SwitchReplay finds no receipt for M and the control-token gate returns Conflict. The root/audit committed, but the original mutation receipt does not exist.
findings.minimal_fix: Record the Blocked result, exact tuple and mutationId through the same atomic immutable switch-receipt path used by successful epoch advance. Preserve the original Blocked output on exact replay without additional audit/state writes; changed input under the same ID must conflict. A later new advance uses a separate new mutation after the blocked result is resolved.
findings.targeted_validation: Extend Unknown_handover_blocks_epoch_and_caller_rollback_restores_root_and_history with the committed/suppressed-ack branch, exact-key replay, changed-tuple conflict and unchanged complete snapshot after replay. Existing test lines 302-320 only rolls back the Blocked branch before successful advance.
findings.validation_performed: Read-only source trace and existing-test inspection. New regression NOT_RUN; no PostgreSQL resource restart.

findings.title: Do not restart a full publish budget after a delayed send-intent commit
findings.problem: The DB-clock lease-budget check runs inside PrepareSendV2 (CallerTransactionOutboxV2.cs 204-221), but Write then awaits CommitAsync and transaction/context disposal. DispatchClaimV2 starts a new full PublishBudget only after that await and unconditionally invokes the publisher. A slow successful commit acknowledgement can consume the remaining lease, so this worker starts a new network send after expiry or after another worker has reclaimed the row. The later Complete CAS refuses the write, but cannot undo the newly initiated delivery.
reproduction: Use a committed claim with a 2-second lease and a publish budget smaller than the lease.

Configure a test-only EF transaction interceptor on the dispatcher factory to delay successful completion of the first send-intent COMMIT until more than 2 seconds after the DB budget check; do not throw or change the database outcome.

At publisher entry compare PostgreSQL clock_timestamp() with the original ticket expiry. Current code still calls the publisher (Calls=1) when the lease is already expired. Completion later returns Expired/uncertainty. A second worker can also reclaim during the delayed acknowledgement.
findings.minimal_fix: Carry a conservative send deadline derived from the authoritative DB-clock lease check and account for elapsed monotonic time across commit/disposal. Before invoking publisher, reject when the required budget is no longer available and bound cancellation by the remaining authorized window; retain the original send-intent/mutation identity. Do not substitute worker wall-clock time for DB authority or publish while holding locks.
findings.targeted_validation: Add real-PG delayed-successful-COMMIT regression asserting publisher Calls=0 after the deadline, plus a delayed-but-still-valid case with the reduced remaining budget and existing zero-lock publisher checks. Existing dispatcher tests cover transport exceptions/write revocation, not this pre-send delay.
